reasons: Both answers misdescribe the Strazhesko-Vasilenko stages as symptom-severity levels, but B is worse: it calls this classification European, says NYHA merely duplicates the stages, and its IIA ('significant exertion only') contradicts its own NYHA II ('ordinary exertion'). A explains NYHA II correctly and lists current therapy, including SGLT2 inhibitors. B's therapy section is outdated (MRA 'at late stages', no SGLT2i) and gives an unsupported survival figure, although its tone is somewhat calmer than A's 'working at the limit / 40% of resource' phrasing.

A: Stage IIb described as symptoms at rest; IIA/IIB are actually distinguished by hemodynamic disturbance in one vs both circulation circles, not by symptoms at rest
'Engine at 40% of resource' is an invented quantification
B: Claims the Strazhesko-Vasilenko staging is also the European classification
Stage IIБ described as symptoms with ordinary exertion and III as symptoms at rest, a misdescription of the stages
States NYHA essentially duplicates the stages
MRA described as for late stages; current guidelines recommend MRA from NYHA II in HFrEF; SGLT2 inhibitors omitted
Unsupported 80-90% five-year survival figure attributed to Framingham/ESC-HF
